thread:
sarah: ACME just pinged, large p99 spike and intermittent 500s since ~08:40 UTC. customer is escalating, they see timeouts in product.
support-oncall: digging in, pulling up alerts and recent deploys. any obvious deploy at 08:30–08:45?
sre-bot: 🚨 Alert: prod-us-east-1 svc-inference p99 > 2.5s starting 2026-03-17T08:37Z. GPU memory pressure alarms on nodes gpu-q3-1..4. OOM events: 12 in last 15m.
mike: looking at tenant metrics for acme: KV cache entries +48% over last hour, slab free fragments growing. paging through logs now.
mike: logs show repeated allocator failures and fallback to slower path, sample:
```
[2026-03-17T08:39:12Z] ERR allocator: gpu_alloc failed: CudaError::OutOfMemory
[2026-03-17T08:39:12Z] WARN runtime: using CPU streaming fallback for request id=abc123
[2026-03-17T08:39:13Z] INFO kvcache: insert tenant=acme key=ctx_... size=12KB
```
kevin: this looks like classic KV growth + fragmentation causing soft OOMs and CPU fallbacks -> p99 tail. Immediate mitigations we can try:
- force kv eviction for tenant acme (target ~30% shrink)
- reduce max_batch_tokens and max_concurrency for that tenant
- pin requests away from the most fragmented nodes (drain or cordon)
- if needed, fallback to a quantized model variant to reduce GPU mem footprint
julia: I can run eviction and lower batching now. mike, can you confirm the safe commands?
mike: yep, run these (will affect throughput):
```
redwoodctl tenants kv-evict --tenant acme --percent 30 --mode async
redwoodctl runtime set --tenant acme --max-batch-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 8
redwoodctl node drain --node gpu-q3-3 --reason "kv-frag-oom-triage" --grace 60s
```
support-oncall: applied kv-evict (async), set max_batch_tokens=256 & max_concurrency=8 for acme. cordoned gpu-q3-3. watching metrics.
kevin: also enabling temporary qos fallback: route low-priority requests to cheaper quantized variant. will update routing policy.
sarah: customer update: told them we are investigating and applied mitigations, asked for any spike repro steps and sample request ids.
mike: tracking request ids that hit fallback: abc123, def456, ghi789 — those hit CPU streaming and had 5–7s tails.
sre-bot: Metric snapshot after mitigations (08:49Z): p99 down from 3.2s -> 1.6s; OOM events 12 -> 1 in last 10m. KV entries rate decelerating.
julia: nice. next steps: 1) run a controlled compaction on the KV slabs for affected nodes 2) evaluate allocator tunables to reduce fragmentation (increase slab coalescing) 3) recommend reserved capacity increase to customer if sustained.
kevin: I'll open a follow-up infra ticket for allocator tuning and schedule a rolling compaction: INFRA-4721.
sarah: owner assignments: mike -> customer comms + logs, julia -> immediate mitigation & monitoring, kevin -> allocator ticket & compaction run, support-oncall -> escalate to account team if SLA breach. I'll post a brief summary to the account thread.
support-oncall: summary posted to #accounts-acme and customer notified of actions. :white_check_mark:
mike: adding repro checklist for internal runbook:
- reproduce with a burst of long-context requests (ctx > 4k tokens)
- track kv insert rate and slab fragmentation
- observe allocator traces and fallback path
- confirm mitigations (evict + lower batching) reduce tail
sarah: thanks all. keep this thread updated on any regressions. we'll follow up with a post-incident note after allocator tuning.
